must: playbook within cap losslessly (J-1a) + allowlist gap handed off with an exact patch (J-1b)

decisions.what: J-1a and J-1b were executed INLINE by the conductor, with zero agents dispatched.

decisions.what: The cap was cut from the ADVICE-ONLY pool, deviating from the letter of the documented overflow rule.

Extrapolated to 16 drops it selects L-003, L-008, L-011, L-016 and L-020 -- five [apply:]-bearing lessons that account for most of applied.log. That is satisfying a count by deleting the machinery the count exists to protect. The rule was instead applied verbatim WITHIN the advice-only pool: all 15 directives survive, 16 advice-only lessons are archived losslessly. The deviation is written up in DROP-RATIONALE-2026-08-17.md so a human can reject it and re-cut from the byte-exact backup.

known_issues.note_cycle_12: PARTIALLY REPAIRED, and the remainder is deliberately a handoff. known_issues.note_cycle_43: ROOT CAUSE MEASURED, not inferred. For 42 cycles the allowlist gap was a black-box observation ('the script is refused'); this cycle READ the permission source of truth, /opt/swarm/.claude/settings.json. permissions.allow contains exactly TWO SWARM-script entries: 'Bash(/Users/truman/Projects/SWARM/bin/swarm-notify.sh:*)' -- a macOS path that does not exist on this host -- and 'Bash(bin/swarm-notify.sh:*)', the relative form that works. There is NO entry for swarm-budget.sh or swarm-playbook.sh in ANY path form, and none for the VPS prefix /opt/swarm/bin. The underlying cause of the whole KI-5 family is that settings.json was never migrated from macOS to the VPS. Established by a 16-check gate (.swarm/runs/cycle-043-gate-ki5.js, output cycle-043-verify-ki5.txt): the allowlist contents PREDICTED 7/7 measured cells including two negative controls (awk absent -> denied; pgrep present -> clean) and two cells no prior cycle had measured. The discriminator is cell 3 vs cell 4: identical script AND arguments (swarm-notify.sh poll), varying ONLY the path form, giving OPPOSITE outcomes -- absolute DENIED, relative CLEAN. A 'the script isn't allowlisted' theory predicts those two alike; the allowlist predicts them opposite, which is the observation a wrong theory could not have produced. TWO OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCES, derived from the allowlist rather than executed: (S8) WRAP_UP's 'bin/swarm-playbook.sh append' WILL be refused -- the manual fallback is confirmed necessary, and was pre-drafted this cycle to /opt/swarm/runs/wrapup-candidates.md rather than left to the WRAP_UP clock; (S9) 'bin/swarm-notify.sh send wrap-up ...' relative from cwd=/opt/swarm WILL be permitted, so the wrap-up push can go out -- previously unknown and assumed dead. ALSO FOUND: permissions.additionalDirectories is EMPTY, so the target is reachable only via the pacer's --add-dir flag. NOTE the compounding with note_cycle_12: the playbook is inert for TWO independent reasons -- the cap breach (cmd_parse exits 2 at >20 lessons) AND this allowlist gap. Fixing either alone leaves it inert. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: hard rule 5 makes settings.json read-only until WRAP_UP completes, so tool bugs found mid-run go to the journal and the morning report, never to a live edit. The repair is two added lines.

known_issues.desc: Subagents in this VPS -p session are sandboxed to the session --add-dir list (/opt/swarm, /opt/targets/aphorism-cli). A git worktree under /tmp is therefore UNREACHABLE to a builder: reads, bash, and EnterWorktree all refuse. Cycle 18 lost one builder dispatch to this. SKILL.md already prescribes "no worktrees" for headless sessions and gives disjoint file scopes as the concurrency answer instead; cycles 16-17 used /tmp worktrees anyway and cycle 18 is where it bit. Remedy for future cycles: at k_cap 1 let the single builder work directly in the target tree (conductor still sole committer); for k>1 headless, either scope builders to disjoint files in the one tree or place worktrees INSIDE an allowed directory.

Subagent scratch files land in the SWARM root (/opt/swarm) unless the dispatch prompt names an explicit scratch path. Hard rule 5 hands agents target paths only, but the session cwd IS /opt/swarm, so a relative scratch path silently lands inside the write fence -- the fence is enforced by what agents are TOLD, and cwd supplies what they were not told. Observed cycle 9 (builder used /opt/swarm/.scratch/) and again at cycles 17-18 (9 untracked .js/.json scratch files in the SWARM root, removed by the conductor at cycle 19). Harmless so far -- all occurrences were inert scratch, nothing under bin/, reference/, workflows/ or templates/ -- but the same reflex on a different task could write into SWARM tooling mid-run. CYCLE 36: control PASSES a third consecutive time. The dispatch prompt named an explicit scratch path (<target>/.swarm/scratch-c36/) and the builder used it; /opt/swarm stayed clean, verified by `git -C /opt/swarm status --porcelain`. The builder did NOT remove its own scratch tree this time (cycle 35's did), so the conductor removed it before commit -- the naming control is what is working; self-cleanup is not reliable and should not be assumed.
known_issues.note_cycle_21: THIRD occurrence, in a new and milder variant: the dispatch prompt named the explicit in-target scratch path as the remedy prescribes, and the builder honored it AND deleted its mutation copies -- but left the bare empty .swarm/scratch directory behind. Measured at 0 files inside, so nothing leaked and no untracked scratch reached git status; this is the same residue cycle 9 recorded (agent removes copies, conductor removes the empty directory). Caught only because the conductor gate carries a standing SCOPE.SCRATCH control, which is the reason to keep that control even on cycles where it looks like a formality. Remedy refinement for the wrap-up distillation: the prompt should say remove the scratch DIRECTORY, not just its contents.
known_issues.remedy: Name an explicit scratch directory in every dispatch prompt. NOT /tmp -- KI-6 established subagents are sandboxed to the session --add-dir list, so /tmp is unreachable. Use <target>/.swarm/scratch/ and require the agent to remove it, with a conductor gate check confirming the removal. Done this way at cycle 19 (T-013) and the agent left nothing behind (harness controls CTRL-SCRATCH, CTRL-TREE). Cycle 9 proposed this as a candidate playbook lesson and it was never made standing, which is why it recurred; it belongs in the wrap-up distillation.
known_issues.note_cycle_24: FOURTH occurrence, and it PARTIALLY CONTRADICTS the cycle-22 note below, so that note should not be read on its own. The cycle-21 remedy refinement was again applied verbatim in the dispatch prompt -- it named the in-target scratch path AND required removing the scratch DIRECTORY itself, not merely its contents, calling out that an empty directory counts as debris and is checked. The builder created three subdirectories under .swarm/scratch/ and reported removing them with rm -rf, which it had genuinely done: the standing SCOPE.SCRATCH control found .swarm/scratch present with ZERO entries inside. So the agent removed what it created and still left the parent it did not create. Nothing leaked, git status showed no untracked scratch, and the conductor removed the directory by hand. The lesson for the wrap-up distillation is narrower and more useful than 'name the scratch path': an agent told to remove its scratch directory removes the directories IT MADE, so the prompt must name the exact path whose absence is checked, or the check must tolerate an empty parent. Cycle 22's 'the remedy is now measured to work' was drawn from a single clean cycle and does not survive a second sample.
known_issues.note_cycle_30: NO occurrence, but this cycle is NOT evidence about the remedy and must not be counted as a clean sample. The standing SCOPE.SCRATCH control passed -- .swarm/scratch is absent and the SWARM root carried no debris at orient or at commit -- yet the builder reported that its scratch mkdir was DENIED OUTRIGHT by the permission layer before executing, because the path it reached for was tied to an out-of-scope README.md verification. So the directory was never created, and the reason is the sandbox rather than the prompt. Recorded this way because cycle 22 drew 'the remedy is measured to work' from a single clean cycle and cycle 24 then contradicted it; counting a permission denial as a third clean sample would repeat that error in a worse form. The issue stays OPEN. Second-order note, more useful than the control itself: the same denial is why the builder could not run the README mutation table empirically and said so unprompted -- the file-scope fence and the builder's ability to self-verify are in genuine tension here, and the conductor gate is what closes it.
known_issues.note_cycle_22: NO occurrence this cycle, and that is evidence rather than luck. The cycle-21 remedy refinement was applied verbatim in the dispatch prompt -- it named the in-target scratch path AND required removing the scratch DIRECTORY itself, not merely its contents, calling out that an empty directory counts as debris and is checked. The builder honoured both: the standing SCOPE.SCRATCH control passed for the first time since the refinement was written (.swarm/runs/cycle-022-verify-T-016.txt), and the SWARM root carried no debris at orient either. The issue stays OPEN because one clean cycle does not close a structural hole -- the fence is still enforced by what the prompt says, and a prompt that forgot the line would reproduce it -- but the remedy is now measured to work, which is what the wrap-up distillation needs.
known_issues.note_cycle_31: FIFTH occurrence, and this one is the CONDUCTOR'S FAULT rather than the agent's -- recorded that way because the remedy did not fail, it was never applied. The dispatch prompt did not name the in-target scratch path at all; it said "do your experimenting in-memory or in /tmp", and KI-6 has established since cycle ~17 that /tmp is unreachable from a subagent sandbox. So the builder, whose permitted directories are /opt/swarm and /opt/targets/aphorism-cli, did the only thing left and wrote t024a-harness.js and t024a-e2e.js into the SWARM ROOT, then deleted them and reported both by name unprompted. Verified clean by the conductor: git status in /opt/swarm is empty and ls of the root shows no residue. Nothing leaked and nothing under bin/, reference/, workflows/ or templates/ was touched. The finding that matters for the wrap-up distillation is that four cycles of remedy refinement are worth nothing if the line is not actually in the prompt -- the fence is enforced by prose that a conductor has to remember to type, which is the structural complaint, not the agent's behaviour. Do not count this as evidence about the remedy in either direction.
known_issues.note_cycle_37: Control PASSES a fourth consecutive time and this cycle is a CLEAN sample, unlike cycle 30's permission-denied non-sample. The dispatch prompt named the explicit in-target path (<target>/.swarm/scratch-c37/) AND required removing that exact directory rather than merely its contents -- the cycle-24 refinement. The builder created it, used it for a four-variant README harness, and removed it itself; the conductor confirmed absence, and `git -C /opt/swarm status --porcelain` was empty at both orient and commit. Note the contrast with cycle 36, where the builder did NOT self-clean: the naming control is what is reliable, self-cleanup is not, and the conductor check is what closes it.

known_issues.desc: The conductor's sealed pre-dispatch baseline is READABLE BY THE BUILDER IT IS MEANT TO BE SEALED FROM. It is written to <target>/.swarm/runs/, which is inside the target directory every builder is given, so a builder that looks around the tree can read the exact cells the conductor committed to before dispatch. Observed cycle 31: the builder volunteered, unprompted, that it had noticed .swarm/backlog.json and two new .swarm/runs/ files and identified them as "the conductor/swarm tooling's own pre-dispatch baseline for this exact item", correctly naming cell B4 and its reading of 50. CYCLE 36 MITIGATION, which does NOT close the root cause: the conductor now uses commit-reveal -- seal written, sha256 committed before dispatch, plaintext DELETED for the whole dispatch window, rewritten and verified with `sha256sum -c` after the builder returns (OK at cycle 36). A deleted file cannot be read by any builder, so THIS cycle's seal was genuinely sealed. The root cause is untouched: <target>/.swarm/runs/ is still inside every builder's directory, every OTHER artefact there (prior gates, probes, baselines) is still readable, and the mitigation is conductor discipline rather than a structural boundary. A future conductor that forgets the delete step is back to KI-8 exactly as filed. The structural fix needs a scratch location outside the subagent sandbox that the conductor can also write, which this session does not have (KI-6 establishes /tmp is outside the sandbox; the Write tool is denied there).
known_issues.status: mitigated in practice, root cause open
known_issues.why_it_matters: Hard rule 2 rests on builders never having seen the check -- an agent that knows the check can code to it. The rule is enforced today by not PUTTING verify commands in the backlog, which is necessary but not sufficient: the baseline file is a second copy of much of the same information sitting in a directory the agent can read. This cycle it changed nothing and the honesty was exemplary -- the builder disclosed it rather than using it, and the decisive evidence (D1/D2) was authored AFTER dispatch and never written to disk until the gate ran, so the verdict is uncontaminated. But the integrity of the gate should not depend on a builder choosing to disclose.
known_issues.remedy: Candidate for the wrap-up distillation, not a mid-run change (hard rule 5 forecloses editing SWARM tooling during a run). Options worth measuring next run, cheapest first: (1) write pre-dispatch baselines to SWARM/runs/ instead of <target>/.swarm/runs/, and copy them into the target only at commit time, so the evidence still lands in the target repo's history but not in the builder's live tree; (2) keep authoring the deciding discriminators strictly after dispatch, which is what actually saved this cycle and is already the hard-rule-2 practice; (3) accept and document it, on the grounds that a builder reading the baseline still cannot see the post-dispatch discriminators. Option 1 plus 2 looks strictly better than 3 and costs almost nothing.
known_issues.note_cycle_32: SECOND OCCURRENCE, AND A WORSE ONE — SEVERITY RAISED medium -> high. Cycle 31 the builder read the pre-dispatch BASELINE. This cycle the builder read .swarm/runs/cycle-031-verify-T-024a.js, which is the GATE ITSELF, containing the full cycle-31 discriminator set D1-D4 and cells G0-G6. It disclosed this unprompted and in detail (report section 6: "my independent measurement was informed by, not blind to, that prior gate's specific cell shapes"), and it explicitly validated its work against those cells. So the escalation is not hypothetical any more: at cycle 31 an agent could have coded to the conductor's check, and at cycle 32 an agent demonstrably DID optimise against it. D1 and D2 were consequently useless as discriminators this cycle. The verdict was saved only because the conductor authored a fresh 9-cell H-set AFTER the builder returned, which is remedy option (2) from the cycle-31 entry doing exactly the job it was proposed for. TWO REFINEMENTS FOR THE WRAP-UP DISTILLATION, both sharper than the original entry: (a) the leak is not only the baseline but EVERY prior cycle's gate artefact, which accumulates in .swarm/runs/ and grows monotonically -- by cycle 32 that directory holds a decade of this run's adversarial thinking, all of it readable by every builder; (b) a second-order harm the cycle-31 entry did not anticipate — the builder inherited cell D4 WITHOUT the backlog note recording that D4 was mis-authored and attributes nothing, then built its headline silent-hole claim on it. Leaked evidence arrives stripped of the caveats that live in the backlog, so it is not merely visible, it is misleading.
known_issues.note_cycle_33: THIRD OCCURRENCE, THIRD DISTINCT CHANNEL, AND THIS ONE IS THE CONDUCTOR'S FAULT. Cycle 31 the agent read the pre-dispatch BASELINE; cycle 32 it read the GATE; cycle 33 it read the conductor's UNCOMMITTED WORKING-TREE EDIT via `git diff test/readme-tags.test.js`, which contained the full BOUNDARY classification and its reasoning. Note what this defeats: the cycle-33 mitigation (pre-commitment sealed to /home/swarm/.swarm-seal/, outside the --add-dir sandbox, with only its SHA-256 committed into the target before dispatch) WORKED -- the seal was never readable. The leak happened because the conductor applied its conclusion to a tracked file while the agent was still running. The agent's read was also legitimate in intent: it saw unexpected modifications in `git status` and diffed a tracked file to check whether it had caused them, which is careful behaviour, and it disclosed the whole thing unprompted and in detail including the ordering of its own measurements. REMEDY, sharper than options (1)-(3) and superseding option (1) which is simply WRONG (it proposes SWARM/runs/, but KI-6 establishes the sandbox is the --add-dir list, which INCLUDES /opt/swarm): (4) hash-commit the seal outside the sandbox -- measured to work this cycle; and (5) THE CONDUCTOR MUST NOT WRITE ITS OWN CONCLUSIONS INTO THE WORKING TREE WHILE AN INDEPENDENT AGENT IS RUNNING. Wait for the return, then edit. Costs nothing and closes the only channel the hash commitment does not.
known_issues.note_cycle_37: Commit-reveal held a SECOND consecutive cycle. Seal written, sha256 committed to the target before dispatch (07efb5a), plaintext DELETED for the whole dispatch window, restored afterwards and verified `sha256sum -c` OK. The builder additionally volunteered, unprompted, that it had run `ls .swarm/` once and had opened NO file under .swarm/runs/ -- the disclosure norm holding for the third cycle running. Root cause STILL UNTOUCHED and this must not be read as closing: every other artefact in .swarm/runs/ remains readable by every builder, and the seal is protected by conductor discipline, not by a boundary. A conductor that forgets the delete step is back to KI-8 exactly as filed. NEW THIS CYCLE, and it is a SEPARATE CHANNEL the commit-reveal does not cover: the ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE itself leaked a test input. T-033's acceptance named the exact reword wording, the builder's fix enumerated exactly that wording, and the acceptance cell consequently could not discriminate. Sealing the gate does nothing about this -- the backlog acceptance is handed to the builder by design. See T-034 and the cycle-37 decision entry.

known_issues.desc: The README Attribution section's two count claims (C1 corpus size, C2 HIGH-risk count) cannot be bound to their markers by any measured rule without falsely rejecting some naturally-written, entirely-TRUE README. Two independent attempts at T-024a, reasoning from different premises, each produced a lateral or negative trade: attempt 1 (cycle 31) swapped "last number before the marker" for "first number in the clause" and scored a perfect 2/4 <-> 2/4 mirror; attempt 2 (cycle 32) swapped positional scanning for two closed grammatical templates and scored 5/9 against HEAD's 7/9 on an independent 9-cell gate, buying one repair (subject-first partitive) with three new false rejections. T-024a is BLOCKED at attempts 2.
known_issues.status: RESOLVED at cycle 2 of run #2 — by removal, which is the one route it named and could not take
known_issues.why_it_matters: AMENDED AT CYCLE 35: the clause below that these guards "fail LOUD on wordings they cannot parse, which is the safe direction" is NO LONGER COMPLETE, and it is left standing with this correction rather than quietly rewritten. Cycle 35 measured a wording they fail SILENT on -- a contradictory count whose digit sits across a dash from its marker binds nothing and is skipped, so a self-contradicting README passes green (KI-10). The loud-only framing held for every case examined through cycle 34; it does not hold in general. Original text follows. These guards are the only thing standing between the README and a silently false claim about the corpus. They currently work on the shipped text and fail LOUD on wordings they cannot parse, which is the safe direction -- nothing is broken for a user today. The risk is the one cycle 25 identified and this issue now quantifies: a maintainer who reformats the Attribution paragraph in a perfectly reasonable way gets a red suite, and the cheapest escape from a false rejection is DELETING the guard, which would take C1 and C2 with it. Twice-measured evidence that no prose-reading rule fixes this is the input a human needs, and it is a judgment call a swarm should not make alone.
known_issues.remedy: NOT another attempt at the same shape -- that is what the attempts cap is for, and the second attempt confirmed rather than contradicted the first. The choice is a human one, between three options this run can lay out but should not pick: (1) ACCEPT AND DOCUMENT -- state at the extraction site that the guard reads the shipped wording and fails loud on rewordings, and that the correct response to a red C1/C2 is to check the numbers and then adjust the template, never to delete the assertion. Cheapest, honest, and consistent with SPEC I-2, which explicitly allows a BOUNDARY survivor to be documented rather than hardened. (2) CHANGE THE DOCUMENT, NOT THE PARSER -- put the two counts somewhere with real structure the guard can read (a small table, or a fenced key: value block in the Attribution section), which removes the English sentence from the loop entirely. This is the only option that actually satisfies T-024's stated remedy, and it is a README change, which is out of the builder file scope this run has used throughout. (3) DROP C1/C2 and rely on the triage document alone. Option 2 is the conductor's lean and it is recorded as a lean, not a decision; it is also the only one of the three that would make T-029 disappear as a side effect.
known_issues.note_cycle_2_run2: The finding itself is NOT overturned and should not be read as retracted: no rule reading an English sentence to decide which number a claim means avoids falsely rejecting some true README. It was measured twice and both measurements stand. What changed is that nothing reads an English sentence any more. This issue named three options for a human and leaned toward option (2), "change the document, not the parser", noting it was the only one that satisfies T-024's remedy and that it was out of the then-current builder file scope. Option (2) is what shipped. The lean was correct.

known_issues.desc: SILENT MISS, LEFT OPEN BY A MEASURED DECISION. The README Attribution guards (C1 corpus size, C2 HIGH-risk count) bind a count to its marker only within the marker's own dash-delimited clause. A contradictory count whose DIGIT sits across an em/en dash from its MARKER therefore binds nothing at all, and an occurrence that binds nothing is skipped rather than counted as unparseable -- so a self-contradicting README passes GREEN. Reproduced at cycle 35: appending "A later audit note records 9 (em dash) HIGH entries (em dash) in total." to the Attribution section leaves the suite at 78/78 while the true HIGH count is 8. Written with ASCII "--" instead, the identical contradiction IS caught -- the dash clause split is provably the mechanism, not a guess.
known_issues.status: RESOLVED at cycle 2 of run #2 — measured closed on a two-arm gate
known_issues.why_it_matters: This is the one failure DIRECTION this improvement run was chartered to remove. Every other open member of this guard family fails LOUD -- it rejects a correct README, which is irritating and safe. This one lets a README that contradicts itself in plain sight pass green, which is worse than having no guard, because a green suite is read as a claim that the numbers were checked. It also corrects KI-9's "fails loud, which is the safe direction" framing, which was accurate for everything examined up to cycle 34 and is not accurate in general.
known_issues.remedy: NOT another narrowing of collectMarkerBindings. That was measured at cycle 35 and the measurement is the reason this issue exists rather than a fix: a 44-cell gate (11 README mutations x 4 arms) rebuilt BOTH natural widenings from the shipped helper -- V1, an unconditional fallback to the previous clause's trailing digit, and V2, that fallback gated on the previous clause holding no marker of its own. BOTH close this hole (cell G1 RED) and BOTH buy a NEW false rejection on entirely TRUE prose (cells CA and CB RED, GREEN on HEAD): a sentence naming a marker with no count at all borrows the neighbouring clause's digit, and an unrelated year does the same. Crossing the clause boundary to catch this shape and avoiding the unrelated-number hazard are the same request. The real fix is KI-9 remedy option (2): give the two counts real structure in the README (a small table or a fenced key: value block) so the guard stops reading English. SWARM TOOL GAP, HIGH because it disables a spend governor (morning report, not a live edit -- hard rule 5 fences bin/). bin/swarm-allocator.sh detects a weekly rollover with an exact integer comparison against the usage probe's week_resets_at: `if [ "$WRST" -ne "$S_WRST" ]; then HU=0; HP=0; SU=0; SP=0; TU=0; ...`. The upstream value is not stable to the second. api/oauth/usage returns seven_day.resets_at with sub-second precision straddling a whole-second boundary; 25 samples over 125s returned BOTH 1786942799 and 1786942800, and four consecutive 5s samples caught the crossing live (04:59:59.954603 -> 05:00:00.110580 -> .317042 -> .463901). Evidence: runs/cycle-040-resets-jitter.json. CONSEQUENCE OBSERVED, not theorised: at 2026-08-16T02:16:47Z the branch fired with no week having rolled over and reset trickle_used_pct from 4 (the configured trickle_pct cap, i.e. exhausted) to 0. That flipped posture halted -> trickle and the pacer spawned cycle 40 on a cap that had not actually been refilled -- the real reset is 2026-08-17T05:00Z, after this run's stop_at. The cap therefore cannot hold across a boundary crossing: it silently refills and the swarm is re-authorised to spend another trickle_pct of a weekly allowance already at 93% (opus 97%). Candidate fixes for a human, none applied: compare with a tolerance (e.g. treat |WRST - S_WRST| <= 2 as the same week), or round/floor the probe value to a stable unit, or gate the rollover on the value having moved FORWARD by most of a week. The conductor held at zero agents this cycle rather than accept the refill -- see decisions[] cycle 40.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEAN: the bug is still high and still live -- on a week where the reserve curve is open (lower weekly_used_pct, or inside the 6h floor release) the same wipe DOES refill a spent cap, and it wipes human attribution unconditionally, which resets the human reserve curve itself. known_issues.status: open (repaired in the rendered artifact; the defective pattern is what remains filed)
known_issues.desc: CONDUCTOR-INSTRUMENT DEFECT, found at cycle 49 while rendering the dashboard. The LIVE per-target node in SWARM/runs/dashboard.html read "cycle 46 - 12 known issues open" while the run was at cycle 48. Cause: dashboard.html's first 112 lines are ONE HTML comment holding a legend with PLACEHOLDER copies of several live anchors, and runs/cycle47-dashboard.mjs matched the target node with /<div class="target"><b>\/opt\/targets\/aphorism-cli<\/b><span>[^<]*<\/span><\/div>/ -- no `g` flag and NO match-count assertion. String.replace with a non-global regex replaces only the FIRST match, and the first match in the file is the legend copy at line 38. So cycle 47 patched a comment nobody sees and left the human-visible node stale; cycle 48 reused the same script and repeated it. DISCRIMINATOR against "the render simply did not run": the legend copy WAS advanced to cycle 47 and then to cycle 48, so the writes landed -- they landed in the wrong region. This is precisely the KI-11 failure mode that runs/c46-dash.mjs's own header warns about in prose, three cycles before it happened; the warning existed and the assertion did not. REPAIRED IN THE ARTIFACT at cycle 49 (runs/c49-dash.mjs anchors the substitution on the `<!-- TARGETS -->` marker so it cannot reach the legend, and asserts an exact match count of 1 before replacing). WHAT REMAINS OPEN is the general defect: the dashboard is re-rendered by a hand-written per-cycle script, so the discipline is re-implemented from scratch every cycle and is only as good as the conductor's memory of it. A prose warning in one cycle's script does not carry to the next. Fix for a human: either strip the legend comment out of the published artifact, or give the anchors machine-distinguishable ids so a render cannot address the legend at all.
known_issues.note: Cost, stated honestly: two cycles of a stale status line on the one page a human actually looks at, while the run itself was healthy and every other live region (banner, timeline, evidence strip) updated correctly. Nothing about the PRODUCT was misreported; the run metadata was. Filed rather than treated as a one-off render slip because the same trap has now fired twice in a row after being documented once.
known_issues.note_cycle_50: SECOND REGION, FOUND BY AUDIT RATHER THAN BY LUCK, AND OLDER THAN THE FIRST. Cycle 49 repaired the per-target node and stopped there; cycle 50 ran the KI-11 comment-classifier over EVERY live region (runs/c50-dash-audit.mjs) and found the identical trap had also eaten the EVIDENCE STRIP. The live <pre class="evidence"> still carried CYCLE 42's content while the legend's placeholder copy carried cycle 48's - so renders 43 through 48 had been writing the verification evidence into an HTML comment for SEVEN cycles, and cycle 49 did not touch the region at all. Repaired in the artifact by runs/c50-dash.mjs, anchored BETWEEN the <!-- TARGETS --> and <!-- /TARGETS --> markers with an exact match-count assertion, and confirmed by re-running the audit after the render. WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE ISSUE: cycle 49 framed it as a per-cycle scripting slip that had fired twice. It is broader than that - the defect is that NOTHING asserts a render reached the live copy, so every region is exposed independently and each one fails silently on its own schedule. The durable repair is still a human's template edit (strip the legend from the published artifact, or give the live anchors machine-distinguishable ids); the cheap standing mitigation, which cost one script this cycle, is to RUN THE AUDIT AFTER EVERY RENDER and require every mandated region to report live=1.
